typeScaleMeta.note: TWO display ramps ship: diarie.dev's, and the brand book's (the bok-* steps in DESIGN.md typography.scale), the latter larger because it is a specimen document. brand/foundations.html briefly carried a third and was converged onto documented steps on 2026-07-29 — bok-omslag for the wordmark, bok-exit-numeral for the exit numerals, and the mellanrubrik / lasare-detalj roles for headings and micro-labels. It adds no steps of its own. Store row diarie-rmp asked whether the remaining two should converge as well; that is still open, and is a narrower question than it was, since diarie.dev and the brand book are genuinely different surfaces.

narrative.overview: diarie is a task tracker that is just files — no daemon, no database, the CLI a reader over YAML the user's editor writes. The identity holds one anchor and two motifs. Anchor: the diarium, the Swedish public registry — every record numbered, findable, never hidden. Motifs: the herbarium (Linné's specimen sheets: 280-year-old plain files; the pressed twinflower mark) and genomlysning (the archivist's light table; in Swedish also the word for scrutiny — the halo is backlighting, not aura). The register is honest, so the design is honest: consequences are named, contrast ratios are computed and published, costs are stated with their revival triggers.
keyCharacteristics: One anchor, two motifs — anything untraceable to them does not belong
Depth is light, never shadow: four flat stepped rings, one permitted box-shadow
Two typefaces mapped to two audiences: serif is the human, mono is the machine
Every accent is the exit-code contract rendered — no decorative colour
Contrast computed and published, not asserted
One easing curve; at most three motion beats per page

rules.name: The Reference-Size Rule
rules.body: A token fontSize is where its axis settings were chosen or where the role tops out — not a size you must ship literally. Ship the fluid role when type has to survive a viewport.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Running prose is capped by one class — .measure (44rem, 64ch) and its centred twin .measure-c. Never author a per-paragraph max-width.

rules.name: The Five-Ink Rule
rules.body: Terminal ink is five classes: .c prompt, .g phosphor, .k structure, .a staleness, .r error. The set is the exit-code contract rendered, so shipping four costs a semantic role rather than a colour.

rules.name: The Verbatim Rule
rules.body: Every terminal block on a brand surface is a claim about the tool's contract and no gate checks it. Generate the text by running the binary, paste the bytes, never truncate with an ellipsis.

rules.name: The Tint-Is-Not-Meaning Rule
rules.body: A card's tint may never be the only thing saying which card it is. Both borders measure below the 3:1 non-text floor (blad-ljus 1.66:1, stampel-dov 1.92:1 on papper), so the state lives in the label — blad-mork at 6.80:1, stampel-mork at 4.89:1 on their own grounds. Read in greyscale, or by a reader who cannot separate the two hues, the cards must still be unambiguous.

dos: Do use stepped light at any scale
Do keep static grain at or below 5%
Do name the consequence, not the adjective
Do state a cost with its revival trigger
Do set mono for anything a machine said
Do name every z-index from the three-value scale
donts: Don't use a gradient glow — the halo is stepped or it is not the halo
Don't make a mascot of the twinflower; it is a specimen
Don't animate on or near a call to action
Don't introduce a second easing curve
Don't put a brand asset behind a login
